definitions.explanation: One's own personal or private business, as opposed to public or work matters. Often used to preface a personal remark.

examples.japanese: {私事|わたくしごと}で{恐縮|きょうしゅく}ですが、{来月|らいげつ}{結婚|けっこん}します。
examples.english: If I may share a personal matter, I'm getting married next month.

examples.japanese: {仕事|しごと}に{私事|わたくしごと}を{持|も}ち{込|こ}まない。
examples.english: to not bring personal matters into work.

examples.japanese: {私事|わたくしごと}を{理由|りゆう}に{会社|かいしゃ}を{休|やす}むのは{気|き}が{引|ひ}ける。
examples.english: I feel reluctant to take time off work for personal reasons.

notes:
A polite, slightly formal word for one's own private affairs. The set phrase {私事|わたくしごと}で{恐縮|きょうしゅく}ですが humbly introduces a personal topic, often in a speech.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {私事|わたくしごと}で{恐縮|きょうしゅく}ですが: if I may mention a personal matter
- {私事|わたくしごと}を{持|も}ち{込|こ}む: to bring in personal matters

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {私事|しじ}: the same kanji read しじ — also 'private affairs,' more bookish
- {公事|こうじ}: public or official matters — the antonym
